transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sam Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO, SummitTrust), Emily Park (Head of ML), Raj Patel (Infra Lead), Linda Gomez (Procurement)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved) capacity. Customer evaluates tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated, needs strong isolation for PII, burst strategy for peak end-of-month volume, and predictable costs for forecasting. Agreed to share sizing and run benchmarks.

[00:00] Sam Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Sam, AE, and Priya is our SE focusing on Dedicated deployments.
[00:12] Michael Torres: Thanks Sam, yeah, appreciate you fitting us in. We wanted to get into dedicated capacity options, basically, we have a couple prod use cases for document summarization and a chat assistant and we're trying to decide if hosted or dedicated makes sense.
[00:26] Priya Nair: great. can you give us a sense of current traffic shape? p50/p95 latency targets? and any regulatory constraints?
[00:33] Emily Park: sure. Right now, our prototype runs on public hosted APIs but we see about 15 qps average during business hours, spiking to around 110 qps during month-end closing windows. Average sequence length across prompts is about 600 tokens, sometimes up to 2k for long doc summaries. Latency target is p95 under 600ms for the chat use case, and the batch doc jobs are okay with higher latency but need throughput.
[01:05] Raj Patel: Also, we have strict data isolation rules - can't have any customer PII leaked to multi-tenant environments. Our security team is asking specifically about VPC, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs and retention.
[01:18] Sam Lee: totally understood. So Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and isolation; with Redwood Private we can go VPC or on-prem, but Dedicated within our cloud provides isolated pools per customer with encryption at rest and KMS integrations, plus audit trails. there are some nuances depending on whether you want a private control plane or not.
[01:35] Michael Torres: what's the difference again between Dedicated and Private? the names blur a bit for us.
[01:40] Priya Nair: short version: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's infrastructure - you get dedicated GPU pools and tenancy isolation within our managed environment. Private is where we hand over more control: private control plane, customer VPC peering or on-prem installers for air-gapped setups. Private is usually for full regulatory or data residency requirements. Dedicated is usually enough when isolation plus contractual SLAs are the ask.
[02:05] Emily Park: ok that's helpful. Our compliance team is leaning toward Dedicated if we can have customer-managed KMS and SOC2/ISO evidence and RBAC.
[02:13] Sam Lee: yes we support CMK/KMS integrations and SOC2 Type II reports; we can share the security pack.
[02:20] Linda Gomez: from procurement angle, we need predictable monthly costs and clear overage/burst pricing. How does Redwood handle burst capacity? sometimes we need to double throughput during end-of-month spikes.
[02:33] Priya Nair: good question. Dedicated includes options for burst/buffer capacity - you can reserve a baseline and configure burst pools that consume unused capacity or allow temporary autoscaling on pre-negotiated rates. there's also a continuous batching strategy to improve utilization while keeping p95 latency targets. For large spikes like your 7x scenario, we often recommend a combination: baseline reserved GPUs sized to average load plus a burst commit that can be used during month end.
[02:58] Raj Patel: how quickly does the burst capacity kick in? and is it pre-provisioned or cold start?
[03:04] Priya Nair: we have two modes: hot burst (warm instances kept ready) which is immediate but has a higher monthly cost, and cold burst (scale-up on demand) which can take minutes depending on region and instance type. for your p95 latency target, we'd recommend hot burst for the model shards that serve chat paths, and cold burst for longer background summarization jobs.
[03:26] Michael Torres: what about model selection? are we locked to specific quantized variants? we run some proprietary fine-tuned models.
[03:33] Sam Lee: you can bring your own fine-tuned weights; Redwood supports pinned versions and model variants. For high throughput we provide quantized execution paths and can recommend a quantization profile that balances latency and quality. for strict accuracy we can run tests to measure regressions.
[03:52] Emily Park: and how does KV cache/prefix caching work? we have a lot of repeated system prompts.
[03:58] Priya Nair: we support prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute, especially for chat. That can significantly reduce cost for repeated context like system prompts and canned instructions. We'll include suggestions in the sizing doc.
[04:12] Raj Patel: security: SSO, SAML, RBAC granularity, and audit logs - can we get real-time logs to our SIEM?
[04:20] Sam Lee: yes SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure streaming and stored for your retention window. We'll include the mechanics in the security pack.
[04:32] Michael Torres: latency: you mentioned p95 can be tuned - is that mostly infra or model? we worry that quantization will hurt output quality for legal docs.
[04:41] Priya Nair: it's both. infra choices (GPU type, batching, KV cache) affect latency; model variant selection affects quality. for legal documents we typically recommend higher precision (non-8-bit quant) variants with slightly more GPU resources. We'll run evals on your prompt set to measure quality vs latency tradeoffs - that's part of the pilot.
[05:00] Linda Gomez: procurement question: what's the minimum contract term for Dedicated and are there penalty clauses for unused capacity?
[05:07] Sam Lee: standard Dedicated contracts are 12 months with committed capacity, but we can discuss 6- or 24-month terms. Unused capacity credits and flexible burst pools can be negotiated. we'll surface standard terms in the pricing packet.
[05:19] Emily Park: on benchmarks - what does Redwood need from us to run a realistic benchmark?
[05:24] Priya Nair: ideally: representative prompt set (we don't need customer data, can use redacted samples), traffic shape (qps by time buckets), target SLAs, and any fine-tuned weights. We'll run parity runs comparing hosted vs dedicated and provide token-level latency/cost breakdowns.
[05:39] Michael Torres: what's a realistic timeline to pilot? we want to run this in July if possible.
[05:45] Sam Lee: timeline looks doable. if we get your workload stats this week, Priya can prepare a benchmark plan and we can schedule a run next week. pilot typically takes 2-3 weeks for full bench and evaluation.
[05:56] Raj Patel: connectivity: do you support private peering and IP allowlists? we can't expose internal endpoints to the public net.
[06:02] Priya Nair: yes we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allowlists. For Dedicated we can provision a private endpoint and peering - if you need the private control plane that's the Private offering; for many customers dedicated with peering suffices.
[06:18] Michael Torres: any limitations on model size for Dedicated? like 70B+ models?
[06:23] Priya Nair: we support up to LLMs that fit on our multi-GPU setups; for really large models we use sharding and model parallelism. we'll include specific GPU family guidance in the sizing doc (A100/H100 equivalent).
[06:36] Emily Park: cost considerations - can we get a rough ballpark for a baseline plus burst? even a ballpark per 1k tokens.
[06:43] Sam Lee: we'll provide formal pricing in the packet, but very high level: Dedicated reserved baseline is priced by GPU hour commitments; per-token costs for serving depend on model variant and batching. We'll include examples: baseline monthly cost for a small pool (e.g., 4x A100-equivalent) plus hot burst to 12 GPUs and expected per-token rates for your prompt mixes.
[07:04] Linda Gomez: procurement will want a worksheet that shows monthly cost sensitivity to burst hours - can you provide that?
[07:09] Sam Lee: absolutely - Priya will include a benchmarking/spreadsheet that shows cost vs usage scenarios.
[07:16] Priya Nair: quick note: we sometimes recommend a canary rollout and A/B traffic split to validate model variants under load before shifting all traffic; Redwood Console supports route-level rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if SLA degrades.
[07:30] Raj Patel: If we use hot burst, what's the process to request more burst? is it automatic?
[07:34] Priya Nair: it can be automated or manual. automation is via autoscaling policies you define (e.g., queue length or p95 triggers) with budget caps and guardrails. We can show a sample policy.
[07:45] Michael Torres: any references of other banks using Dedicated? helps the case.
[07:49] Sam Lee: yes, we've worked with a few financial customers (we can share anonymized case studies). We'll include one pager in the pack.
[07:58] Emily Park: ok, sounds good. Are there any red flags we should know of?
[08:03] Priya Nair: only practical stuff: accurate traffic shape matters a lot for sizing; also for very bursty workloads cold start scaling can add minutes so if you need sub-second p95 you need warm resources for those endpoints. We'll make explicit recommendations.
[08:18] Michael Torres: perfect. Let's confirm next steps and owners.

Recap / Next steps:
- Sam to send Dedicated pricing and sizing options + standard contract terms (Sam Lee)
- Priya to prepare benchmark plan and shared spreadsheet showing cost sensitivity and recommended GPU families (Priya Nair)
- SummitTrust (Raj/Emily) to provide workload stats and representative prompts (Raj Patel / Emily Park)
- Schedule infra deep-dive and benchmark run for next week

[08:50] Linda Gomez: procurement note - we'll need SOC2 and liability limits in the contract.
[08:55] Sam Lee: understood, will include SOC2 pack and discuss terms.
[09:00] Michael Torres: thanks everyone; we'll get the stats over by Friday.
[09:05] Sam Lee: great, appreciate it. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the packet.

End of call.
